title: Longest Strictly Increasing Subsequence With Non-Zero Bitwise AND
summary: Given an integer array, find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence where the bitwise AND of the elements is non-zero.
statement: Given an integer array, find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence where the bitwise AND of the elements is non-zero. If no such subsequence exists, return 0.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 nonnegative values.
Choose a strictly increasing subsequence whose cumulative bitwise AND is nonzero.
Return its maximum length, or zero if none exists.
hints: A nonzero AND means at least one bit is set in every chosen value.
For each possible bit, filter values containing it and compute their strictly increasing LIS.
Take the maximum LIS length over all bit positions.
Every valid subsequence shares some set bit and appears in that bit’s filtered sequence; every filtered LIS has nonzero AND at that bit.
editorial: Every valid subsequence shares some set bit and appears in that bit’s filtered sequence; every filtered LIS has nonzero AND at that bit.

tests.explanation: Subsequence [5,7] is increasing and has AND five, so length two is attainable.
All three increase and share bit one, giving length three.
